editorial:
Imagine your husband suddenly quits his stable job because he thinks he is the next great novelist. That is exactly the mess you get into here. You will meet a husband who is so blinded by his own dreams that he forgets his family needs to eat. To keep the lights on, his wife has to step into the spotlight as a Broadway dancer. It is a funny, lighthearted look at role reversal and the stress of trying to make it big in the city. The vibe is very classic Old Hollywood, filled with fast talking and silly misunderstandings that will keep you smiling.

What really works here is the chemistry between the leads and the snappy pacing. While some of the jokes feel a bit dated, the heart of the story still hits home today. You will love the costume changes and the energy of the dance scenes. If you are into vintage comedies, you should definitely track this one down. Since it is an older film, you might find it as a digital rental on Apple TV, but for the best experience, try to find a high-quality restoration to add to your physical collection. It is a great pick for a cozy movie night with the family.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the couple has to face the truth about their careers and their growing family. After all the fighting and jealousy over her dancing career, the husband finally realizes that his ego almost cost him everything. He stops focusing only on his book and puts his wife first. They reconcile their marriage and decide to face the challenges of parenthood together, ending the movie on a happy, loving note.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school romantic comedies and Broadway flair.
